# Hacker Courses

> The online courses programmers keep recommending, ranked from 3,371 public Hacker News comments, 2006 to October 2026: 1,376 courses with a page each.

Each course is scored from who recommended it, how strongly, in how many separate threads and for how many years (one vote per person; replies piling onto one thread are damped). Every course page quotes the comments behind its ranking and links each one to Hacker News. The catalog, rankings and summaries are CC BY 4.0; please cite and link the course page. Not affiliated with Y Combinator or Hacker News.

## Courses by topic

- [Machine Learning & AI](https://hackercourses.com/topic/machine-learning-and-ai/): 172 courses. Top: Machine Learning (Andrew Ng), Practical Deep Learning for Coders, CS231n: Convolutional Neural Networks for Visual Recognition, Deep Learning Specialization (Andrew Ng), Neural Networks for Machine Learning (Geoffrey Hinton)
- [Algorithms & Data Structures](https://hackercourses.com/topic/algorithms-and-data-structures/): 78 courses. Top: Algorithms, Part I, CS61A: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs, 6.006 Introduction to Algorithms, Introduction to Computer Science and Programming in Python, Algorithms: Design and Analysis, Part 1
- [CS Fundamentals & Systems](https://hackercourses.com/topic/cs-fundamentals-and-systems/): 166 courses. Top: The Elements of Computing Systems (Nand2Tetris), CS50: Introduction to Computer Science, Human Behavioral Biology (Robert Sapolsky), 6.824 Distributed Systems, 15-213 Introduction to Computer Systems
- [Mathematics](https://hackercourses.com/topic/mathematics/): 178 courses. Top: 18.06 Linear Algebra (Gilbert Strang), Stat 110: Probability, The Theoretical Minimum (Leonard Susskind), 6.042J Mathematics for Computer Science, Essence of Linear Algebra
- [Programming Languages](https://hackercourses.com/topic/programming-languages/): 124 courses. Top: 6.001 Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs, Functional Programming Principles in Scala, Programming Languages (Dan Grossman), Design of Computer Programs, Compilers
- [Web & Mobile Development](https://hackercourses.com/topic/web-and-mobile-development/): 131 courses. Top: CS193P Developing Applications for iOS using SwiftUI, CS253 Web Development, Web Development, CSS for JavaScript Developers, The Web Developer Bootcamp
- [Databases & Data Engineering](https://hackercourses.com/topic/databases-and-data-engineering/): 30 courses. Top: 15-445/645 Intro to Database Systems, Introduction to Databases, 15-721 Advanced Database Systems, Intro to Database Systems, Databases: 5 SQL (Stanford)
- [Security & Cryptography](https://hackercourses.com/topic/security-and-cryptography/): 25 courses. Top: Cryptography I, Applied Cryptography, CS255 Introduction to Cryptography (Dan Boneh), Modern Binary Exploitation, Securing Digital Democracy
- [Science & Engineering](https://hackercourses.com/topic/science-and-engineering/): 150 courses. Top: Introduction to Biology - The Secret of Life, The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Underactuated Robotics, For the Love of Physics (Walter Lewin), 6.002 Circuits and Electronics
- [Business, Finance & Economics](https://hackercourses.com/topic/business-finance-and-economics/): 91 courses. Top: Economics of Money and Banking, Financial Markets, Behavioral Economics (Dan Ariely), How to Start a Startup, Startup Engineering
- [Design & Creative](https://hackercourses.com/topic/design-and-creative/): 31 courses. Top: Pixar in a Box, Writing Science Fiction and Fantasy (Brandon Sanderson), How to Draw, Introduction to Human-Computer Interaction, Songwriting
- [Humanities & Social Science](https://hackercourses.com/topic/humanities-and-social-science/): 154 courses. Top: Justice (Michael Sandel), How to Listen to and Understand Great Music, Personality and its Transformations (Jordan Peterson), A Brief History of Humankind, The Peloponnesian War
- [General Learning](https://hackercourses.com/topic/general-learning/): 46 courses. Top: Learning How to Learn: Powerful mental tools to help you master tough subjects, Model Thinking, The Science of Well-Being, How to Speak, The Art of Doing Science and Engineering (Richard Hamming)
